import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 50

*References:*
* [erdosproblems.com/50](https://www.erdosproblems.com/50)
* [Er95] Erdős, Paul, Some of my favourite problems in number theory, combinatorics, and geometry.
Resenhas (1995), 165-186.
* [Sch38] Schoenberg, I. J. "On asymptotic distributions of arithmetical functions."
Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 39.2 (1936): 315-330.
-/

open Filter Set MeasureTheory Topology
open scoped Nat Topology

namespace Erdos50

/--
A function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is the asymptotic distribution function of the values
of $\varphi(n)/n$ if for all $c \in [0, 1]$, the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$
exists and equals $f(c)$.
-/
def IsDistributionOfPhiRatio (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, {n : ℕ | (φ n : ℝ) < c * n}.HasDensity (f c)

/--
A monotone function $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is purely singular (or singular continuous)
if it is continuous and its derivative equals zero almost everywhere with respect to Lebesgue
measure.
-/
def IsPurelySingular (f : ℝ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  Continuous f ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂volume, deriv f x = 0

/--
Schoenberg [Sch38] proved that the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$ exists.
That is, for any $c \in [0, 1]$, the proportion of integers $n \le N$ satisfying $\varphi(n)/n < c$
approaches a limit as $N \to \infty$. This limit function is the cumulative distribution function
of the values of $\varphi(n)/n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_50_schoenberg : ∃ f : ℝ → ℝ, IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős [Er95] proved that the distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$ is purely singular: it is
continuous, but its derivative is zero almost everywhere.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_50_singular (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f) : IsPurelySingular f := by
  sorry

/--
Let $f$ be the asymptotic distribution function of $\varphi(n)/n$, so that for each $c \in [0,1]$,
$f(c)$ is the natural density of $\{n : \varphi(n) < cn\}$. Is it true that there is no $x$ such
that the derivative $f'(x)$ exists and is positive?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_50 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᵉ (f : ℝ → ℝ) (hf : IsDistributionOfPhiRatio f),
    ¬∃ x ∈ Icc (0 : ℝ) 1, ∃ y > 0, HasDerivWithinAt f y (Icc 0 1) x := by
  sorry

end Erdos50

findings.description: The conclusion asserts singularity on all of ℝ, but the hypothesis specifies f only on [0,1]. In particular, `IsPurelySingular f` requires `Continuous f` globally. Given any admissible f, retain its values on [0,1], set g(2) = 1, and set g = 0 in a punctured neighborhood of 2. Then `IsDistributionOfPhiRatio g` still holds, while g is discontinuous at 2. Thus, given Schoenberg's existence result, the universally quantified singularity claim is false. This is a genuine domain mismatch, not a status issue.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, [Er95], p. 171, §I.9: “the density of the integers for which φ(n)/n < c exists for every c (0 ≤ c ≤ 1). I proved that the distribution function is purely singular.” This concerns the distribution on its specified interval (or its canonical constant extension), not arbitrary extensions outside that interval. Primary text: https://www.revistas.usp.br/resenhasimeusp/article/download/74798/78366 .
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict the conclusion to [0,1], for example `ContinuousOn f (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1) ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(volume.restrict (Icc (0 : ℝ) 1)), HasDerivWithinAt f 0 (Icc 0 1) x`. Alternatively, strengthen `IsDistributionOfPhiRatio` to require the density equality for every real c, which forces the canonical values 0 below the interval and 1 above it and makes the global singularity statement appropriate.

reformulations.difference: The source names the distribution function f, whereas Lean universally quantifies over every real function satisfying the interval-density predicate.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any two admissible functions agree on [0,1], by uniqueness of each natural-density limit. For x in [0,1], `HasDerivWithinAt f y (Icc 0 1) x` depends only on that restriction. Consequently the universal statement is equivalent to the same derivative question for any one fixed admissible function. Schoenberg's existence result ensures there is such a function. Unlike the global singularity conclusion, this statement is unaffected by arbitrary extensions outside the interval.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/50 — status and remarks read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/50; direct access returned a Cloudflare challenge.

Paul Erdős, Some of my Favourite Problems in Number Theory, Combinatorics, and Geometry, Resenhas (1995), 165–186, especially p. 171, §I.9. https://www.revistas.usp.br/resenhasimeusp/article/download/74798/78366
Rényi Institute's collected-papers index: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/ and https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/Erdos.html

Repository review conventions: STATEMENTS.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, and AGENTS.md; relevant density/answer definitions and Mathlib totient, cardinality, derivative, monotone-function, and Lebesgue-measure sources.
Local calibration material: both not_misformalizations cases; past_misformalizations INDEX.md and examples pr00054, pr00179, pr00434, pr00565, pr00576, and pr01138.
review.notes: Checked all five declarations. The website still records the main question as OPEN, and Er95 explicitly asks about a finite positive derivative, matching the real-valued derivative witness. Scratch proofs in /workspace/review/scope.lean establish the bad extension, refute the singularity claim conditional on distribution existence, and prove the main quantifier equivalence; their axiom lists contain no sorryAx. Boundary tests in inspect.lean and boundaries.lean verify the totient conventions, exclusion of n = 0, the strict threshold at 1/2, f(0) = 0, f(1) = 1, and derivative uniqueness at both interval endpoints. The full Schoenberg paper could not be retrieved from AMS/JSTOR; its metadata and opening excerpt were checked, and its stated existence result is explicitly corroborated by the primary Er95 passage. No repository files were edited.

demonstrated.claim: Using the file’s Schoenberg existence theorem, changing f(2) preserves the density hypothesis, but the original function and its one-point modification cannot both be globally continuous, refuting the exact theorem type.

submission.summary: Created /workspace/review/trivial_proof.lean with a short proof of ¬ (type_of% @Erdos50.erdos_50_singular). The requested compile command completed with no errors or warnings; the proof explicitly uses the imported Schoenberg existence theorem.

trivial_proof.lean:
import FormalConjectures.ErdosProblems.«50»

/-! The only existence input is the imported Schoenberg theorem. -/

open Filter Set Topology

-- Erdos50.erdos_50_singular is false: changing f(2) preserves the density
-- hypothesis, but f and its one-point modification cannot both be continuous.
example : ¬ (type_of% @Erdos50.erdos_50_singular) := by
  classical
  intro h
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := Erdos50.erdos_50_schoenberg
  let g : ℝ → ℝ := Function.update f 2 (f 2 + 1)
  have hg : Erdos50.IsDistributionOfPhiRatio g := by
    intro c hc
    have hc2 : c ≠ 2 := by linarith [hc.2]
    simpa [g, Function.update_of_ne hc2] using hf c hc
  have hlim : Tendsto f (𝓝[≠] (2 : ℝ)) (𝓝 (f 2 + 1)) :=
    continuousAt_update_same.mp ((h g hg).1.continuousAt (x := 2))
  have heq : f 2 = f 2 + 1 := tendsto_nhds_unique
    ((h f hf).1.continuousAt.tendsto.mono_left nhdsWithin_le_nhds) hlim
  linarith

submission.summary: Restricted the conclusion to continuity on [0,1] and an actual zero within-derivative almost everywhere with respect to Lebesgue measure restricted to that interval. Updated the docstring accordingly and left all other declarations unchanged. Compilation succeeds with only the existing `sorry` warnings.
